pages.x: Charles II of Spain, sickly from birth and called the Bewitched, had no children. When he died in 1700 he left his whole empire, Spain, much of Italy, the Spanish Netherlands and the Americas, to Philip, the grandson of Louis XIV of France. England, the Dutch and Austria feared France and Spain would become one superpower.

Louis XIV accepted the will, and his grandson became Philip V of Spain. Now, someone at Versailles is said to have declared, there are no more Pyrenees. In 1701 England, the Dutch Republic and the Austrian emperor formed a Grand Alliance against France.

In 1704 the Duke of Marlborough, England's greatest general, marched his army 400 kilometres from the Low Countries to the Danube, joined Prince Eugene of Savoy, and smashed a French and Bavarian army at Blenheim, France's first great defeat in forty years. A grateful queen gave him a palace, named Blenheim.
Also in 1704 an English and Dutch fleet captured Gibraltar, the rock at the mouth of the Mediterranean. Britain kept it, and it is still British today, though Spain wants it back.

The war spread from Spain to Italy, Germany, the Low Countries and the Americas. At Malplaquet in 1709, the bloodiest battle of the century, the allies won but lost twice as many men as the French. France itself was starving after the great frost of that winter.

pages.x: In 1711 the Habsburg claimant to Spain became emperor, and his allies had no wish to see him rule Spain too. By the peace of 1713 and 1714 Philip kept Spain and its colonies but gave up any claim to France, Austria took Spain's lands in Italy and the Netherlands, and Britain won Gibraltar, Minorca and the right to sell enslaved Africans in Spanish America.

The war kept France and Spain apart, and set up a balance of power that shaped Europe for a century. Philip's Bourbon family still holds the Spanish throne. Britain came out as a great naval and trading power, on its way to ruling the waves.
pts: Europe fought to keep France and Spain apart
